record.what_it_does: Work management platform with sheets, projects, automation, reports and dashboards.
record.auth_notes: Multi-user apps use 3-legged OAuth 2.0. Apps are registered in Developer Tools, which issues a client ID and secret and requires at least one access scope. Single-user or machine-to-machine use can rely on a personal API access token sent as a Bearer header. The hosted MCP server accepts either OAuth 2.0 or a personal access token.
record.access_notes: Generating an API access token needs a Business, Enterprise or Advanced Work Management plan. Registering for Developer Tools (needed for OAuth apps) needs an email that belongs to a licensed user on Business or higher, and Smartsheet may deny the request. No free developer account or sandbox was found. Publishing an app is an opt-in setting that makes its profile page public; the docs describe no formal app-review step. Whether a 30-day Business trial can register for Developer Tools is unverified.
record.api_breadth_notes: Covers sheets, rows, columns, cells, attachments, discussions and comments, workspaces, folders, reports, dashboards (sights), users, groups, webhooks, search and more. Regional hosts exist for US, EU and AU. A downloadable OpenAPI spec is at developers.smartsheet.com/_bundle/api/smartsheet/openapi.yaml.
record.mcp_notes: Official hosted MCP server at https://mcp.smartsheet.com (US), https://mcp.smartsheet.eu (EU) and https://mcp.smartsheet.au (AU). It went GA on March 24, 2026, authenticates with OAuth 2.0 or a personal access token, and needs a Business, Enterprise or AWM plan. The older local repo, smartsheet-platform/smar-mcp on GitHub, is deprecated in favour of the hosted server.
record.blocker_notes: Getting an API token, registering an OAuth app in Developer Tools and using the MCP server all need a licensed Business-or-higher account. No free sandbox exists. Once you have a paid seat, OAuth app registration is self-serve with no documented review.
